propositions: Multiple git bundle objects for a single S3 ref cause hard clones to fail ('multiple updates for ref not allowed') and block pushes, leaving the store uncloneable and making git-remote-s3 reject cmd_push before writing any bundle.

Upstream's git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocks on input() prompts at manage.py:137,141) and discards non-chosen heads by default, permanently losing ticket events unique to side-branched heads and violating the append-only invariant.

Multi-bundle state is ordinary ref divergence hidden at git-remote-s3's bundle-storage layer; rebar must detect and heal it autonomously by lossless 2-parent merge (never discard), writing the merged tip before deleting originals to guarantee at least one bundle carries full history at every crash point.

The heal acquires the helper's per-ref conditional-put lock (S3Remote.acquire_lock), re-enumerates bundles (TOCTOU guard), fetches all heads locally, folds them via iterated 2-parent git merges under rebar's write_lock (following sync._union_merge semantics with merge=ours for .bridge_state/*), then writes the merged bundle before deleting originals and releasing the lock.

push_tickets_branch must detect the multi-bundle signature (_is_multi_bundle) before non-FF recovery, invoke heal_multi_bundle exactly once (via healed_once guard), and retry the push so the final bundle carries both local writes and all divergent heads.

The doctor adds no hard S3 SDK dependency to core rebar (boto3 ships transitively with git-remote-s3 under the optional [s3] extra); all S3 access is routed through git-remote-s3's importable S3Remote/.s3 client, imported lazily behind require_s3_helper().
